text: A flat stone and a still stretch of water. {lead} sends it dancing across, once, twice, five times, and something on the far side wobbles loose: Ammonite.
Bubbles rise in the peat. {lead} follows them down and brings up, to its evident pride, Burn Water Flask.
A cheese wheel stuck in a hollow, as they do. {lead} gives it a shove and down the slope it goes, and the hollow gives up Wade Whimsie.
{lead} takes a run up and lofts the bowl clean over the verge. Where it comes down: Cream Tea.
A molehill, freshly heaped. {lead} drums a gentle rhythm on the ground and the worms come up to see what the fuss is. Among the soil: a few coins.
{lead} takes a run up and lofts the bowl clean over the verge. Where it comes down: Toby Jug.
The wheel has been here since last spring's chase. {lead} sets it rolling, and underneath is a few coins.
A flat stone and a still stretch of water. {lead} sends it dancing across, once, twice, five times, and something on the far side wobbles loose: Tara Brooch Copy.
The drystone has slumped. {lead} lifts the big stones in first and wedges the small ones after, which is exactly how it is done. Behind the stones: Four-Leaf Clover.
{lead} takes a run up and lofts the bowl clean over the verge. Where it comes down: Lucky Chip.
{lead} tips the wheel over the lip and it bounds off downhill with great purpose. Where it was sitting: a few coins.
A glint under the surface, just out of reach. {lead} hooks it with patience and a bit of reed. It is a purse, a bit damp.
A coracle, left on the bank, light as a basket. {lead} gets in and paddles across without spinning more than twice. On the far side: Norfolk Reed.
The drystone has slumped. {lead} lifts the big stones in first and wedges the small ones after, which is exactly how it is done. Behind the stones: Rowan Sprig.
A molehill, freshly heaped. {lead} drums a gentle rhythm on the ground and the worms come up to see what the fuss is. Among the soil: Bacon Rind.
A gap in the wall, where the stones have gone for a walk. {lead} fits them back one by one, like a very slow jigsaw. Tucked in the wall behind: Hag Stone.
A bale and a bend, and a bowl that wants lofting. {lead} swings and sends it up over the hedge in one long arc. It lands by some loose change and a gratitude card.
A knot of sheep, all facing the wrong way. {lead} works them in a neat curve until the gate is clear. Left on the post for you: a few coins.
Bubbles rise in the peat. {lead} follows them down and brings up, to its evident pride, Ammonite.
{lead} lofts the bowl clear over the hedge and the bale makes a fine step. You scramble over after it, picking out the odd twig.
You go back over the bale, and {lead} lofts the bowl after you. A passing cyclist nods, as if this is normal.
{lead} taps out a steady beat beside the hill and the earth begins to wriggle. Turned up with the worms: Four-Leaf Clover.
